correctness.rationale: For each population size the particle minimum is exactly a common Brownian motion minus a rescaled maximum of N independent Brownian paths. Uniform-on-compact convergence of those normalized maxima to the square-root curve, justified by finite-grid Gaussian tail bounds and reflection-principle moduli, yields the stated two population limits. Brownian boundary regularity makes first hitting continuous almost surely. Under logarithmic time, the limiting survival event is a stationary Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process above a barrier approaching sqrt(2a); spectral squeezing gives a precise polynomial survival exponent. The positive Dirichlet eigenfunction x^2-1 at boundary x=1 has eigenvalue one, so the limiting first moment is finite exactly at a>1/2. The actual finite-system Gaussian quadratures, Brownian trajectory code and discrete OU spectral computations passed, independently of the analytic arguments.
